//
// Input-fusion wrapper for a pure-elementwise producer fusing into a
// pure-elementwise consumer foreach -- the case that always shares one index
// space. A view on either side is `ViewFuser`'s job.
//
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Dialect/MAPOps.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Support/InputFusion.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Transforms/MAPTransforms.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MODialect/MODevices.h"

#include "mlir/Support/LLVM.h"

using namespace M;

namespace M::MAP {

#define GEN_PASS_DEF_FUSEELEMENTWISE
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Transforms/MAPTransforms.h.inc"

namespace {

// A tensor with more static elements than the threshold (or an unknown element
// count) is "large": re-reading it is expensive (JSC-30 / MSTDL-2759).
bool isLargeTensorOperand(Type type, int64_t largeTensorElementThreshold) {
  auto tensorType = dyn_cast<MO::TensorType>(type);
  if (!tensorType)
    return false;
  std::optional<int64_t> numElements = tensorType.getNumElements();
  return !numElements.has_value() || *numElements > largeTensorElementThreshold;
}

// Cheap to duplicate iff at most one input is a large tensor: duplication
// re-reads all inputs once per extra consumer, a win only when at most one
// re-read is expensive.
bool isCheapToDuplicate(IterElementwiseOp op,
                        int64_t largeTensorElementThreshold) {
  int numLargeOperands = 0;
  for (Value input : op.getInputs())
    if (isLargeTensorOperand(input.getType(), largeTensorElementThreshold))
      if (++numLargeOperands > 1)
        return false;
  return true;
}

struct FuseElementwisePass
    : public MAP::impl::FuseElementwiseBase<FuseElementwisePass> {
  using Base::Base;
  FuseElementwisePass(const FuseElementwisePass &other) : Base(other) {}

  void runOnOperation() override {
    InputFusionConfig config;
    // Both kernels pure elementwise (no index transform).
    config.shouldFuse = [](StoreOp srcStore, LoadOp dstLoad) {
      auto src = srcStore->getParentOfType<IterElementwiseOp>();
      auto dst = dstLoad->getParentOfType<IterElementwiseOp>();
      return src && dst && !isViewForeach(src) && !isViewForeach(dst);
    };
    // Never duplicate a host kernel.
    int64_t threshold = largeTensorElementThreshold;
    config.canDuplicate = [threshold](IterElementwiseOp src) {
      return !MO::isOnHost(src) && isCheapToDuplicate(src, threshold);
    };
    config.maxFusionSetSize = maxFusionSetSize;
    numKernelsFused = fuseInput(getOperation(), config);
  }

  Statistic numKernelsFused{this, "num-kernels-fused",
                            "Number of kernels fused"};
};

} // namespace

} // namespace M::MAP

//
// Output-fusion wrapper for a consumer that reads the producer's result at an
// untransformed index, so e.g. `matmul` followed by a bias `add` becomes one
// kernel whose epilogue computes the add inline. A reshape read is
// `ReshapeEpilogueFuser`'s job.
//
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Dialect/MAPOps.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Support/OutputFusion.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Transforms/MAPTransforms.h"

#define GEN_PASS_DEF_FUSEEPILOGUE
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Transforms/MAPTransforms.h.inc"

namespace {

struct FuseEpiloguePass : public MAP::impl::FuseEpilogueBase<FuseEpiloguePass> {
  using Base::Base;
  FuseEpiloguePass(const FuseEpiloguePass &other) : Base(other) {}

  void runOnOperation() override {
    OutputFusionConfig config;
    config.shouldFuse = [](StoreOp, LoadOp consumerLoad) {
      return consumerReadsUntransformed(consumerLoad);
    };
    numKernelsFused = fuseOutput(getOperation(), config);
  }

  Statistic numKernelsFused{this, "num-kernels-fused",
                            "Number of kernels fused"};
};

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
//
// Fuses MAP kernels by inlining producers into consumers.
//
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Dialect/MAPOps.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Transforms/MAPTransforms.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MODialect/MOOps.h"

#include "mlir/Pass/PassManager.h"
#include "mlir/Transforms/Passes.h"

using namespace M;

namespace M::MAP {

#define GEN_PASS_DEF_FUSEKERNELS
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Transforms/MAPTransforms.h.inc"

namespace {

struct FuseKernelsPass : public MAP::impl::FuseKernelsBase<FuseKernelsPass> {
  using Base::Base;

  void runOnOperation() override {
    MO::GraphOp graphOp = getOperation();

    // One fusion round: input fusion before output fusion, so a
    // view/elementwise producer fuses into a foreach consumer before that
    // consumer is output-fused into an epilogue -- which is what lets a view
    // reach an epilogue without fusing directly into a closure. Prologue runs
    // after elementwise/view so every producer it sees is the maximal
    // elementwise/view chain.
    mlir::OpPassManager fusePm(MO::GraphOp::getOperationName());
    fusePm.addPass(createFuseElementwise());
    fusePm.addPass(createFuseViews());
    fusePm.addPass(createFusePrologue());
    fusePm.addPass(createFuseReductions());
    fusePm.addPass(createFuseEpilogue());
    fusePm.addPass(createFuseReshapeEpilogue());
    // Last, so siblings merge only once the producer-consumer fusers have
    // collapsed what they can this round.
    fusePm.addPass(createFuseHorizontal());

    // Between rounds, only CSE: the fusers dedup the kernels they fused into
    // and erase consumed producers, so a full canonicalization would be wasted
    // work.
    mlir::OpPassManager cleanupPm(MO::GraphOp::getOperationName());
    cleanupPm.addPass(mlir::createCSEPass());

    auto kernelCount = [&] {
      unsigned n = 0;
      graphOp.getBody().walk([&](IterOpInterface) {
        ++n;
        return WalkResult::skip();
      });
      return n;
    };

    // Repeat until a round fuses nothing, since folding one link of a chain can
    // expose the next. Every fusion erases a kernel, so a round that leaves the
    // kernel count unchanged fused nothing.
    unsigned fused;
    do {
      unsigned before = kernelCount();
      if (failed(runPipeline(fusePm, graphOp)))
        return signalPassFailure();
      fused = before - kernelCount();
      numKernelsFused += fused;
      if (failed(runPipeline(cleanupPm, graphOp)))
        return signalPassFailure();
    } while (fused > 0);
  }
};

} // namespace

} // namespace M::MAP

#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Transforms/MAPTransforms.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MODialect/MODevices.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MODialect/MOOps.h"

#include "GraphCompiler/Support/DataflowUtils.h"

using namespace M;

#define DEBUG_TYPE "map-fuse-mutable-loads"

namespace M::MAP {

#define GEN_PASS_DEF_FUSEMUTABLELOADS
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Transforms/MAPTransforms.h.inc"

// Only these kernels take a fused mutable load.
bool isFusibleKernel(Operation *op) {
  return isa_and_present<MAP::IterElementwiseOp, MAP::IterOpaqueOp>(op);
}

/// The kernel to fuse `loadOp` into, or null. The kernel must be the sole
/// consumer of the load's tensor.
Operation *maybeGetCompatibleKernel(MO::MutableLoadOp loadOp) {

  auto tensor = loadOp.getOutTensor();

  if (!tensor.hasOneUse()) {
    LLVM_DEBUG(loadOp.emitRemark()
               << "Mutable load fusion is disabled for this load op as its "
                  "output tensor has more than one use.");

    return nullptr;
  }

  if (loadOp->getBlock() != (*tensor.getUsers().begin())->getBlock()) {
    LLVM_DEBUG(
        loadOp.emitRemark()
        << "Mutable load fusion is disabled for this load op as its "
           "output tensor is produced in a different block than its user.");
    return nullptr;
  }

  Operation *kernelOp = *tensor.getUsers().begin();
  if (!isFusibleKernel(kernelOp))
    return nullptr;

  // Reading the buffer in place of the load's snapshot is only sound if the
  // kernel writes only the element it reads, as map.iter.elementwise does. An
  // in-place map.iter.opaque may write any element.
  if (isa<MAP::IterOpaqueOp>(kernelOp) &&
      llvm::is_contained(kernelOp->getOperands(), loadOp.getInBuffer())) {
    LLVM_DEBUG(loadOp.emitRemark()
               << "Mutable load fusion is disabled for this load op as the "
                  "opaque kernel consuming it also writes its buffer.");
    return nullptr;
  }

  return kernelOp;
}

IterElementwiseOp fuseLoadBufferAndChains(PatternRewriter &rewriter,
                                          MO::MutableLoadOp loadOp,
                                          IterElementwiseOp kernelOp) {
  MLIRContext *ctx = rewriter.getContext();

  auto chainType = MO::ChainType::get(ctx);

  auto &tensorUse = *loadOp.getOutTensor().getUses().begin();
  auto argIdx = tensorUse.getOperandNumber();

  SmallVector<Value> newInputs(kernelOp.getInputs());
  newInputs[argIdx] = loadOp.getInBuffer();

  SmallVector<Type> newResultTypes(TypeRange(kernelOp.getResults()));
  newResultTypes.push_back(chainType);

  rewriter.setInsertionPointAfter(kernelOp);

  auto newKernelOp = IterElementwiseOp::create(
      rewriter, kernelOp->getLoc(),
      /*resultTypes=*/newResultTypes,
      /*shape=*/kernelOp.getShape(),
      /*inputs=*/newInputs,
      /*chain=*/loadOp.getInChain(),
      /*fusionInfo=*/
      MOGG::createFusionInfo<MOGG::FusionMutableLoadAttr>(
          kernelOp->getContext(), {loadOp, kernelOp}),
      /*hasReadEffect=*/true,
      /*hasWriteEffect=*/kernelOp.getHasWriteEffect());

  // Inherent, so `setDiscardableAttrs` below does not carry it.
  newKernelOp.setDispatch(kernelOp.getDispatch());

  newKernelOp->setLoc(mlir::FusedLoc::get(
      kernelOp->getContext(), {loadOp->getLoc(), kernelOp->getLoc()}));
  newKernelOp->setDiscardableAttrs(kernelOp->getDiscardableAttrDictionary());

  // Build the new block with the buffer type at argIdx, then splice the old
  // body in.
  Block &oldBody = kernelOp.getBody().front();
  Block *newBody = &newKernelOp.getBody().emplaceBlock();
  for (auto [i, arg] : llvm::enumerate(oldBody.getArguments())) {
    Type argType = i == argIdx ? loadOp.getInBuffer().getType() : arg.getType();
    newBody->addArgument(argType, arg.getLoc());
  }

  rewriter.cloneRegionBefore(kernelOp.getBody(), newKernelOp.getBody(),
                             newKernelOp.getBody().begin());
  Block &oldBodyClone = newKernelOp.getBody().front();

  SmallVector<Value> fusedArgs(newBody->getArguments().begin(),
                               newBody->getArguments().end());
  rewriter.inlineBlockBefore(&oldBodyClone, newBody, newBody->begin(),
                             fusedArgs);

  auto outChainIdx = newKernelOp.getNumResults() - 1;
  Value outChain = newKernelOp->getResult(outChainIdx);

  loadOp.getOutChain().replaceAllUsesWith(outChain);

  for (auto &&[oldRes, newRes] :
       llvm::zip(kernelOp->getResults(), newKernelOp->getResults())) {
    oldRes.replaceAllUsesWith(newRes);
  }

  kernelOp->erase();
  loadOp->erase();

  return newKernelOp;
}

// When the kernel depends on the load's out-chain, fusing would create a cycle.
// If the path is an exclusive run of single-use `mo.chain.create`s, rewrite
// them to consume the load's in-chain instead; otherwise give up.
//
// BEFORE (fusion blocked):
//   %t, %outCh = mo.mutable.load(buf, %inCh)
//   %merged = mo.chain.create(%other, %outCh)  // kernel depends on %outCh
//   %result = mo.custom(..., %t, %merged)      // can't fuse: creates cycle
//
// AFTER DETACHMENT (fusion enabled):
//   %t, %outCh = mo.mutable.load(buf, %inCh)   // %outCh becomes dead
//   %merged = mo.chain.create(%other, %inCh)   // %outCh -> %inCh
//   %result = map.iter.elementwise(buf, ..., %merged)  // fused!
//     fusionInfo = MutableLoad(...)
//
// Requires: %outCh and %merged have single use (exclusivity constraint).
static bool detachExclusiveChainPath(Value loadOutChain, Value loadInChain,
                                     Value kernelInChain) {
  if (kernelInChain == loadOutChain) {
    return false;
  }

  SmallVector<MO::ChainCreateOp> toRewrite;
  llvm::SmallPtrSet<Operation *, 16> onPath;

  // Returns:
  //   * std::nullopt - this branch never reaches the load's out-chain.
  //   * false        - the branch touches the load but fails exclusivity checks
  //                    (non-chain.create op or extra users).
  //   * true         - the branch is exclusively composed of single-use
  //                    chain.create ops and is safe to rewrite.
  std::function<std::optional<bool>(Value)> analyzeChainValue =
      [&](Value v) -> std::optional<bool> {
    if (v == loadOutChain)
      return true;

    auto chainCreate = v.getDefiningOp<MO::ChainCreateOp>();
    if (!chainCreate)
      return std::nullopt;

    bool subtreeReachesLoad = false;
    for (Value operand : chainCreate.getInputs()) {
      if (operand == loadOutChain) {
        subtreeReachesLoad = true;
        continue;
      }

      if (std::optional<bool> pathStatus = analyzeChainValue(operand)) {
        if (!*pathStatus) {
          return false;
        }
        subtreeReachesLoad = true;
      }
    }

    if (!subtreeReachesLoad) {
      return std::nullopt;
    }

    // Another user would observe the rewiring.
    if (!chainCreate.getResult().hasOneUse()) {
      return false;
    }

    if (onPath.insert(chainCreate.getOperation()).second)
      toRewrite.push_back(chainCreate);

    return true;
  };

  if (analyzeChainValue(kernelInChain) != true)
    return false;

  for (MO::ChainCreateOp chainCreate : toRewrite)
    chainCreate->replaceUsesOfWith(loadOutChain, loadInChain);

  ASSERT_STREAM(!dataflowGraphDependsOn(kernelInChain, loadOutChain),
                "Expected exclusive chain path from mutable.load to kernel op "
                "to be severed.");

  return true;
}

// A prologue capture's block argument mirrors the captured type, so it follows
// the tensor -> buffer retype.
void retypeFusedPrologueCaptures(Value bufferArg) {
  for (OpOperand &use : bufferArg.getUses()) {
    auto prologueOp = dyn_cast<MAP::IterPrologueOp>(use.getOwner());
    if (!prologueOp)
      continue;

    // Block args are [index, captures...].
    prologueOp.getBody()
        .getArgument(use.getOperandNumber() + 1)
        .setType(bufferArg.getType());
  }
}

void fuseLoadBuffer(PatternRewriter &rewriter, MO::MutableLoadOp loadOp,
                    Operation *kernelOp, bool kernelHasLoadsOutputChain) {
  auto buffer = loadOp.getInBuffer();
  auto tensor = loadOp.getOutTensor();

  ASSERT_STREAM(*tensor.getUsers().begin() == kernelOp,
                "Expected value semantic tensor from load op to only be "
                "consumed by current kernel op");

  OpOperand &operand = *tensor.getUses().begin();
  auto argIdx = operand.getOperandNumber();

  auto kernel = cast<IterOpInterface>(kernelOp);
  Block &kernelBody = kernelOp->getRegion(0).front();

  TypedValue<MO::ChainType> loadOutChain = loadOp.getOutChain();
  if (Value kernelInChain = kernel.getInputChain()) {
    if (kernelInChain != loadOutChain &&
        dataflowGraphDependsOn(kernelInChain, loadOutChain) &&
        !detachExclusiveChainPath(loadOutChain, loadOp.getInChain(),
                                  kernelInChain)) {
      LLVM_DEBUG(loadOp.emitRemark() << "Skipping mutable load fusion to avoid "
                                        "introducing a chain cycle.");
      return;
    }
  }

  kernel.insertInputsAt(argIdx, buffer);
  Value newBufferArg = kernelBody.getArgument(argIdx);

  auto oldBlockArg = kernelBody.getArgument(argIdx + 1);
  oldBlockArg.replaceAllUsesWith(newBufferArg);
  kernel.eraseInputsAt(argIdx + 1, 1);

  retypeFusedPrologueCaptures(newBufferArg);

  if (!kernelHasLoadsOutputChain) {
    loadOutChain.replaceAllUsesWith(kernel.getOutputChain());

    rewriter.setInsertionPoint(kernelOp);

    auto newChain = rewriter.createOrFold<MO::ChainCreateOp>(
        loadOp.getLoc(),
        ValueRange{kernel.getInputChain(), loadOp.getInChain()});
    kernel.setChain(newChain);
  } else {
    kernel.setChain(loadOp.getInChain());
  }

  kernel.setFusionInfoAttr(MOGG::createFusionInfo<MOGG::FusionMutableLoadAttr>(
      kernelOp->getContext(), {loadOp, kernelOp}));
  kernelOp->setLoc(mlir::FusedLoc::get(kernelOp->getContext(),
                                       {loadOp->getLoc(), kernelOp->getLoc()}));

  loadOp.erase();
}

// Fuses `loadOp` into a read-only opaque `kernelOp` with no chain, giving it a
// chain in/out pair (GEX-3962). Otherwise the load stays a full-buffer copy,
// e.g. a gather indexing a KV leaf materializes the whole leaf per read.
// `map.iter.opaque` cannot grow results in place, so the op is replaced.
IterOpaqueOp fuseLoadBufferAndChains(PatternRewriter &rewriter,
                                     MO::MutableLoadOp loadOp,
                                     IterOpaqueOp kernelOp) {
  MLIRContext *ctx = rewriter.getContext();
  auto chainType = MO::ChainType::get(ctx);

  OpOperand &tensorUse = *loadOp.getOutTensor().getUses().begin();
  auto argIdx = tensorUse.getOperandNumber();

  SmallVector<Value> newInputs(kernelOp.getInputs());
  newInputs[argIdx] = loadOp.getInBuffer();

  SmallVector<Type> newResultTypes(TypeRange(kernelOp.getResults()));
  newResultTypes.push_back(chainType);

  rewriter.setInsertionPointAfter(kernelOp);
  auto newKernelOp = IterOpaqueOp::create(rewriter, kernelOp.getLoc(),
                                          newResultTypes, newInputs,
                                          /*inputChain=*/loadOp.getInChain(),
                                          /*fusionInfo=*/Attribute());
  newKernelOp.setDeviceRef(MO::getDeviceOrDefaultAny(kernelOp));
  newKernelOp.setHasReadEffect(true);
  newKernelOp.setHasWriteEffect(kernelOp.getHasWriteEffect());
  // Inherent, so `setDiscardableAttrs` below does not carry it.
  newKernelOp.setDispatch(kernelOp.getDispatch());

  newKernelOp->setLoc(
      mlir::FusedLoc::get(ctx, {loadOp->getLoc(), kernelOp->getLoc()}));
  newKernelOp->setDiscardableAttrs(kernelOp->getDiscardableAttrDictionary());

  // The chain has no block argument, so only the fused input is retyped.
  newKernelOp.getBody().takeBody(kernelOp.getBody());
  BlockArgument fusedArg = newKernelOp.getBody().front().getArgument(argIdx);
  fusedArg.setType(loadOp.getInBuffer().getType());
  retypeFusedPrologueCaptures(fusedArg);

  loadOp.getOutChain().replaceAllUsesWith(newKernelOp.getOutputChain());

  for (auto &&[oldRes, newRes] :
       llvm::zip(kernelOp->getResults(), newKernelOp->getResults()))
    oldRes.replaceAllUsesWith(newRes);

  newKernelOp.setFusionInfoAttr(
      MOGG::createFusionInfo<MOGG::FusionMutableLoadAttr>(ctx,
                                                          {loadOp, kernelOp}));

  kernelOp->erase();
  loadOp->erase();

  return newKernelOp;
}

/// Turns a mo.mutable.load op with n uses into n mo.mutable.load ops each with
/// a single use of their value semantic tensor output.
struct ParallelizeLoadsWithMultipleUsers
    : MO::DeviceAwareRewritePattern<OpRewritePattern, MO::MutableLoadOp> {
  ParallelizeLoadsWithMultipleUsers(MLIRContext *ctx)
      : DeviceAwareRewritePattern(ctx, 1) {}

  LogicalResult
  deviceAwareMatchAndRewrite(MO::MutableLoadOp loadOp,
                             MO::DeviceAwareRewriter &rewriter) const override {
    auto tensor = loadOp.getOutTensor();
    auto loadBuffer = loadOp.getInBuffer();

    if (tensor.use_empty() || tensor.hasOneUse()) {
      return rewriter.notifyMatchFailure(
          loadOp.getLoc(),
          "Output value semantic tensor has <= 1 uses, skipping "
          "parallelization pattern.");
    }

    // After splitting, a consumer that writes the buffer would race the other
    // consumers' fused reads.
    for (OpOperand &use : tensor.getUses()) {
      Operation *consumer = use.getOwner();
      auto kernel = dyn_cast<IterOpInterface>(consumer);
      if (!kernel || !kernel.getHasWriteEffect())
        continue;

      if (llvm::is_contained(consumer->getOperands(), loadBuffer)) {
        return rewriter.notifyMatchFailure(
            loadOp.getLoc(),
            "Parallelization blocked: a consumer kernel has write effect and "
            "shares the same buffer as the load operation.");
      }
    }

    auto *loadBlock = loadOp->getBlock();

    for (OpOperand &use : tensor.getUses()) {
      if (use.getOwner()->getBlock() != loadBlock) {
        // TODO(GEX-1203): Add support for cross-block load parallelization
        return rewriter.notifyMatchFailure(
            loadOp.getLoc(),
            "Found use of output tensor in different block than load op, "
            "skipping parallelization to maintain cross-block semantics");
      }
    }

    auto chainType = MO::ChainType::get(loadOp.getContext());
    auto outTensor = loadOp.getOutTensor();

    llvm::SmallVector<Value> chains;
    llvm::SmallVector<OpOperand *> opOperands;
    for (OpOperand &use : outTensor.getUses())
      opOperands.push_back(&use);

    for (OpOperand *use : opOperands) {
      auto newLoadOp = rewriter.create<MO::MutableLoadOp>(
          loadOp.getLoc(), outTensor.getType(), chainType, loadOp.getInBuffer(),
          loadOp.getInChain());

      rewriter.modifyOpInPlace(use->getOwner(), [&newLoadOp, &use]() {
        use->set(newLoadOp.getOutTensor());
      });

      chains.push_back(newLoadOp.getOutChain());
    }

    // Want the generated mo.chain.create to show up in a semi-reasonable spot.
    for (Operation *user : loadOp.getOutChain().getUsers()) {
      rewriter.setInsertionPoint(user);
      break;
    }

    Value newChain =
        rewriter.create<MO::ChainCreateOp>(loadOp.getLoc(), ValueRange{chains});

    rewriter.replaceAllUsesWith(loadOp.getOutChain(), newChain);

    loadOp.erase();

    return success();
  }
};

bool kernelAlreadyHasDirectBufferInput(Operation *kernelOp,
                                       MO::MutableLoadOp loadOp) {
  if (!loadOp.getOutChain().hasOneUse())
    return false;

  auto *user = *loadOp.getOutChain().getUsers().begin();
  if (user != kernelOp)
    return false;

  OpOperand *tensorOperand = nullptr;
  for (OpOperand &opOperand : kernelOp->getOpOperands()) {
    if (opOperand.get() == loadOp.getOutTensor()) {
      tensorOperand = &opOperand;
      break;
    }
  }

  if (!tensorOperand)
    return false;

  unsigned tensorIdx = tensorOperand->getOperandNumber();
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < kernelOp->getNumOperands(); ++i) {
    if (kernelOp->getOperand(i) == loadOp.getInBuffer() && i != tensorIdx)
      return true;
  }

  return false;
}

bool kernelHasInOutChains(Operation *kernelOp) {
  auto kernel = cast<IterOpInterface>(kernelOp);
  return kernel.getInputChain() && kernel.getOutputChain();
}

struct FuseMutableLoads : public impl::FuseMutableLoadsBase<FuseMutableLoads> {
  using FuseMutableLoadsBase::FuseMutableLoadsBase;
  void runOnOperation() override {
    MO::GraphOp moGraph = getOperation();
    MLIRContext *ctx = moGraph->getContext();
    PatternRewriter rewriter{ctx};

    SmallVector<Operation *> opsToProcess;
    moGraph.walk(
        [&](MO::MutableLoadOp loadOp) { opsToProcess.push_back(loadOp); });

    RewritePatternSet patterns{ctx};
    patterns.add<ParallelizeLoadsWithMultipleUsers>(ctx);

    if (failed(
            mlir::applyOpPatternsGreedily(opsToProcess, std::move(patterns))))
      return signalPassFailure();

    LLVM_DEBUG(llvm::dbgs() << "Graph after load parallelization:\n";
               moGraph.print(llvm::dbgs()); llvm::dbgs() << '\n');

    SmallVector<MO::MutableLoadOp> loadOps;
    moGraph.walk([&](MO::MutableLoadOp loadOp) { loadOps.push_back(loadOp); });

    for (auto loadOp : loadOps) {
      Operation *kernelOp = maybeGetCompatibleKernel(loadOp);
      if (!kernelOp)
        continue;

      if (kernelAlreadyHasDirectBufferInput(kernelOp, loadOp)) {
        // TODO: Unify all these cases
        fuseLoadBuffer(rewriter, loadOp, kernelOp,
                       /*kernelHasLoadsOutputChain=*/true);
      } else if (!kernelHasInOutChains(kernelOp)) {
        // The kernel must now both consume and produce a chain.
        //
        // TODO(GEX-1031): Split into adding the chain, then the
        // mo.tensor -> mo.buffer rewrite.
        if (auto foreachOp = dyn_cast<MAP::IterElementwiseOp>(kernelOp))
          fuseLoadBufferAndChains(rewriter, loadOp, foreachOp);
        else
          fuseLoadBufferAndChains(rewriter, loadOp,
                                  cast<MAP::IterOpaqueOp>(kernelOp));
      } else {
        fuseLoadBuffer(rewriter, loadOp, kernelOp,
                       /*kernelHasLoadsOutputChain=*/false);
      }
    }
  }
};

} // namespace M::MAP

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
//
// Merges two sibling foreaches over the same index space that share an input
// into one multi-output kernel, so the shared operand is loaded once. Unlike
// the other fusers this pairs siblings rather than a producer with a consumer.
// It also moves a consumer into its producer's epilogue when the producer's
// result has other readers, which output fusion leaves alone; one that reads a
// strided window of the result runs there under a `map.index.slice.select`.
// An elementwise producer in that position merges with its consumer too,
// keeping its store and handing the consumer the value it computed.
//
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Dialect/MAPOps.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Support/OutputFusion.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Transforms/MAPTransforms.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MODialect/MODevices.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MODialect/MOOps.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/MOGGDialect/Support/FusionUtils.h"
#include "GraphCompiler/Support/DataflowUtils.h"

#include "mlir/IR/IRMapping.h"
#include "mlir/IR/PatternMatch.h"
#include "llvm/ADT/DenseMap.h"
#include "llvm/ADT/STLExtras.h"
#include "llvm/ADT/SetVector.h"

#include <tuple>

using namespace M;

namespace M::MAP {

#define GEN_PASS_DEF_FUSEHORIZONTAL
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Transforms/MAPTransforms.h.inc"

namespace {

// The pair is rebuilt at `b`, so anything between the two that reads `a`'s
// results would end up ahead of its definition. A graph region allows that and
// the dependency walks already rule out a cycle, so this only keeps kernels in
// def-before-use order, conservatively. A reader inside a region (an `mo.if`
// branch) counts against the op that encloses it here, which is what actually
// moves relative to `b`.
bool resultsUnusedBefore(IterElementwiseOp a, IterElementwiseOp b) {
  Block *block = b->getBlock();
  return llvm::none_of(a->getUsers(), [&](Operation *user) {
    Operation *inBlock = block->findAncestorOpInBlock(*user);
    return inBlock && inBlock->isBeforeInBlock(b);
  });
}

// Whether `op`'s body loads from its input `in`.
bool loadsInput(IterElementwiseOp op, Value in) {
  Block &body = op.getBody().front();
  for (auto [i, operand] : llvm::enumerate(op.getInputs()))
    if (operand == in &&
        llvm::any_of(body.getArgument(i).getUsers(),
                     [](Operation *user) { return isa<LoadOp>(user); }))
      return true;
  return false;
}

// The kernels `fusible` can pair: same shape and device, both loading
// `loadedOperand`.
struct FusionCandidateGroup {
  Attribute shape;
  Attribute device;
  Value loadedOperand;

  std::tuple<Attribute, Attribute, Value> key() const {
    return {shape, device, loadedOperand};
  }
  bool operator==(const FusionCandidateGroup &other) const {
    return key() == other.key();
  }
};

// A kernel belongs to one group per operand it loads.
SmallVector<FusionCandidateGroup>
fusionCandidateGroupsOf(IterElementwiseOp op) {
  SmallVector<FusionCandidateGroup> groups;
  for (Value in : op.getInputs()) {
    FusionCandidateGroup group{op.getShapeAttr(), MO::getDeviceOrDefault(op),
                               in};
    if (loadsInput(op, in) && !llvm::is_contained(groups, group))
      groups.push_back(group);
  }
  return groups;
}

bool fusible(IterElementwiseOp a, IterElementwiseOp b) {
  // 1) Check that both kernels have the same shape and device.
  if (a.getShapeAttr() != b.getShapeAttr())
    return false;
  if (MO::getDeviceOrDefault(a) != MO::getDeviceOrDefault(b))
    return false;

  // 2) Skip kernels with side effects (not supported for now).
  // A chain or a memory effect carries an ordering this pass doesn't model.
  if (a.getChain() || b.getChain() || a.getHasReadEffect() ||
      a.getHasWriteEffect() || b.getHasReadEffect() || b.getHasWriteEffect())
    return false;

  // A view chain becomes a zero-copy view after fusion, which a multi-result
  // kernel can't, so merging it would turn a free view into a copy.
  if (isRaisableViewChain(a) || isRaisableViewChain(b))
    return false;

  // 3) Only pair kernels that both load a shared operand.
  // Loading it once is the whole gain. An operand only read as slice bounds
  // (starts/stops/steps, shared by every window slice) saves nothing and would
  // steal the slice from the producer it could fuse into. Most pairs fail here,
  // so this runs before the dependency walks.
  if (!llvm::any_of(a.getInputs(), [&](Value in) {
        return llvm::is_contained(b.getInputs(), in) && loadsInput(a, in) &&
               loadsInput(b, in);
      }))
    return false;

  // 4) Check that no dependency between the 2 kernels makes the fused kernel
  // invalid.
  // The merged kernel takes `b`'s place, so nothing in between may read `a`'s
  // results, and neither kernel may depend on the other, even indirectly, or it
  // would consume its own result.
  if (!resultsUnusedBefore(a, b))
    return false;
  return !dataflowGraphDependsOn(b, a) && !dataflowGraphDependsOn(a, b);
}

// Whether a slice leaves a strided window of its input that no view can
// express -- the only kind worth a select in the producer's kernel. A
// contiguous slice (every step 1, and at most one sliced dim ahead of the
// first non-unit one) is an offset view, better left to view fusion than paid
// for with a second store.
bool isStridedWindow(SliceSpecAttr spec) {
  MOSH::ShapeAttr in = spec.getSignature().getIn();
  MOSH::ShapeAttr out = spec.getSignature().getOut();
  ArrayRef<int64_t> steps = spec.getSteps().asArrayRef();
  if (llvm::any_of(steps, [](int64_t step) { return step != 1; }))
    return true;
  bool nonUnitDimSeen = false;
  for (unsigned d = 0, e = in.getRank(); d < e; ++d) {
    if (in.getValues()[d] != out.getValues()[d] && nonUnitDimSeen)
      return true;
    if (in.getIntDims()[d] != 1)
      nonUnitDimSeen = true;
  }
  return false;
}

// The slice through which a consumer reads the fused operand, when a select
// at `selectIdx` can invert it: one load, through one `map.index.slice` of the
// loop index, in a body with one store at the loop index; a strided window no
// view expresses; and within the select's rules at that index. The body then
// moves into the select, where the loop index is the slice's output index --
// the consumer's own -- so elementwise work between the load and the store
// keeps its meaning there. Null otherwise.
// TODO(slariau): also take loads of the consumer's other inputs at the loop
// index, which the select keeps in bounds; today they decline the merge.
SliceIndexOp matchSelectableSlice(BlockArgument fusionArg,
                                  BlockArgument loopIdx,
                                  ArrayRef<StoreOp> stores, Value selectIdx) {
  if (stores.size() != 1 || !fusionArg.hasOneUse())
    return nullptr;
  StoreOp store = stores.front();
  auto load = dyn_cast<LoadOp>(*fusionArg.getUsers().begin());
  if (!load)
    return nullptr;
  auto slice = load.getIndex().getDefiningOp<SliceIndexOp>();
  if (!slice || slice.getIndex() != loopIdx || !slice->hasOneUse())
    return nullptr;
  if (store.getIndex() != loopIdx)
    return nullptr;
  if (llvm::any_of(loopIdx.getUsers(), [&](Operation *user) {
        return user != slice.getOperation() && user != store.getOperation() &&
               !isa<CallElementwiseOp>(user);
      }))
    return nullptr;
  if (!isStridedWindow(slice.getSpec()) ||
      failed(SliceSelectOp::verifySpecAt(slice.getSpec(), selectIdx)))
    return nullptr;
  return slice;
}

// The producer's own output store and each consumer of that result write one
// element of the same index space, so they are siblings -- but one of them
// sits inside the producer, where `fuse` cannot reach it. So the merge goes
// the other way: the consumer moves into the producer's epilogue and stores
// beside the store already there, which is the one the producer still owes the
// readers fusion cannot absorb. Output fusion will not do this, since it takes
// a result with a single reader.
bool fuseEscapingReader(IterOpaqueOp &dst) {
  for (unsigned idx = 0, e = dst.getNumNonChainResults(); idx < e; ++idx) {
    Value res = dst->getResult(idx);
    if (!isa<MO::TensorType>(res.getType()))
      continue;

    IterElementwiseOp src;
    unsigned numConsumers = 0;
    bool escapes = false;
    for (OpOperand &use : res.getUses()) {
      auto consumer = dyn_cast<IterElementwiseOp>(use.getOwner());
      if (consumer && use.getOwner()->getBlock() == dst->getBlock()) {
        ++numConsumers;
        src = consumer;
        continue;
      }
      escapes = true;
    }
    // Without an escaping reader this is a plain producer/consumer edge that
    // output fusion already takes. More than one consumer waits for `fuse` to
    // merge them with each other first, since moving one in would strand the
    // other behind a producer it can no longer reach.
    if (!escapes || numConsumers != 1)
      continue;
    if (src.getChain() || src.getHasReadEffect() || src.getHasWriteEffect())
      continue;
    if (llvm::count(src.getInputs(), res) != 1)
      continue;
    if (llvm::any_of(src->getResultTypes(),
                     [](Type t) { return !isa<MO::TensorType>(t); }) ||
        llvm::any_of(dst->getResultTypes(),
                     [](Type t) { return !isa<MO::TensorType>(t); }))
      continue;

    IterEpilogueOp epilogueOp = dst.getEpilogueForResult(idx);
    if (!epilogueOp)
      continue;
    Block &epilogueBody = epilogueOp.getBody().front();
    SmallVector<StoreOp> epilogueStores = getOutputStores(epilogueBody);
    Block &srcBody = src.getBody().front();
    SmallVector<StoreOp> srcStores = getOutputStores(srcBody);
    if (epilogueStores.size() != 1 || srcStores.size() != src.getNumResults())
      continue;
    // A select in the consumer moves into the epilogue whole, so it must hold
    // at the epilogue's store index.
    if (llvm::any_of(
            srcBody.getOps<SliceSelectOp>(), [&](SliceSelectOp select) {
              return failed(SliceSelectOp::verifySpecAt(
                  select.getSpec(), epilogueStores.front().getIndex()));
            }))
      continue;

    // The consumer must read the fused operand at its own loop index -- the
    // epilogue hands over one element, with no way to honor a transform --
    // or through a strided slice of it, which a select inverts: the consumer
    // then runs only where the slice selects the element, at its own index.
    unsigned fusionArgIdx =
        llvm::find(src.getInputs(), res) - src.getInputs().begin();
    BlockArgument fusionArg = srcBody.getArgument(fusionArgIdx);
    BlockArgument srcLoopIdx = srcBody.getArguments().back();
    SliceIndexOp slice;
    SliceSpecAttr sliceSpec;
    if (llvm::any_of(fusionArg.getUsers(), [&](Operation *user) {
          auto load = dyn_cast<LoadOp>(user);
          return !load || load.getIndex() != srcLoopIdx;
        })) {
      StoreOp epilogueStore = epilogueStores.front();
      if (!isa<MO::TensorType>(epilogueStore.getTensor().getType()))
        continue;
      // The select would sit at the epilogue store's index, so the merge
      // checks the select's rules there. They reject a transformed index,
      // such as a fused reshape's, which can carry one stored vector across
      // rows of the slice's input.
      slice = matchSelectableSlice(fusionArg, srcLoopIdx, srcStores,
                                   epilogueStore.getIndex());
      if (!slice)
        continue;
      sliceSpec = slice.getSpec();
    }
    // Another operand reaching back through `dst` would make the merge a cycle.
    if (llvm::any_of(src->getOperands(), [&](Value other) {
          return other != res && dataflowGraphDependsOn(other, dst);
        }))
      continue;

    IRRewriter rewriter(dst.getContext());
    unsigned numDpsBefore = dst.getNumNonChainResults();
    dst = growOutputs(dst, src->getResultTypes(), rewriter);
    epilogueOp = dst.getEpilogueForResult(idx);
    Block &body = epilogueOp.getBody().front();

    StoreOp epilogueStore = getOutputStores(body).front();
    Value val = epilogueStore.getValue();
    Value storeIdx = epilogueStore.getIndex();
    Location loc = epilogueStore.getLoc();

    // The fused operand's block arg is a tensor; `val` is already the scalar
    // `dst` produced for this element, so every load of it becomes `val`.
    for (Operation *user : llvm::to_vector(fusionArg.getUsers())) {
      auto load = cast<LoadOp>(user);
      load.getResult().replaceAllUsesWith(val);
      load.erase();
    }
    // The select takes over the slice, spec and all.
    if (slice)
      slice.erase();

    // Every other input the body still reads becomes a capture, threaded
    // through a new input of `dst` -- the epilogue is isolated from above. A
    // slice's bounds tensors are no longer read, since the select carries them
    // statically.
    for (auto [i, input] : llvm::enumerate(src.getInputs())) {
      if (i == fusionArgIdx || srcBody.getArgument(i).use_empty())
        continue;
      unsigned dstInputIdx = dst.getInputs().size();
      dst.insertInputsAt(dstInputIdx, input);
      epilogueOp.getCapturesMutable().append(
          dst.getInputBlockArgs()[dstInputIdx]);
      srcBody.getArgument(i).replaceAllUsesWith(
          body.addArgument(input.getType(), input.getLoc()));
    }

    // The grown output block args are the consumer's destinations.
    SmallVector<Value> caps;
    Block::BlockArgListType outArgs = dst.getOutputBlockArgs();
    for (unsigned i = 0, n = src->getNumResults(); i < n; ++i) {
      BlockArgument outArg = outArgs[numDpsBefore + i];
      epilogueOp.getCapturesMutable().append(outArg);
      caps.push_back(body.addArgument(outArg.getType(), outArg.getLoc()));
    }

    // A store in a select keeps its place and its index, the select's
    // argument; only its destination moves to the new capture. The whole
    // stores are rebuilt at the consumer's index below.
    SmallVector<std::pair<Value, Value>> wholeStores;
    for (auto [store, cap] : llvm::zip_equal(getOutputStores(srcBody), caps)) {
      if (store->getBlock() != &srcBody) {
        store.getTensorMutable().assign(cap);
        continue;
      }
      wholeStores.push_back({cap, store.getValue()});
      store.erase();
    }

    // The producer's own store stays: it is what the escaping reader is owed.
    // Through a slice, the consumer's body moves into a select, which runs it
    // at the slice's index and only where the slice selects the element.
    Block *consumerBody = &body;
    Value consumerIdx = storeIdx;
    if (sliceSpec) {
      rewriter.setInsertionPointToEnd(&body);
      auto select = SliceSelectOp::create(rewriter, loc, sliceSpec, storeIdx);
      consumerBody =
          rewriter.createBlock(&select.getBody(), select.getBody().end(),
                               {storeIdx.getType()}, {loc});
      consumerIdx = consumerBody->getArgument(0);
    }
    srcLoopIdx.replaceAllUsesWith(consumerIdx);
    srcBody.eraseArguments(0, srcBody.getNumArguments());
    rewriter.inlineBlockBefore(&srcBody, consumerBody, consumerBody->end());
    rewriter.setInsertionPointToEnd(consumerBody);
    for (auto [cap, storedVal] : wholeStores)
      StoreOp::create(rewriter, loc, cap, consumerIdx, storedVal);

    SmallVector<Value> replacements;
    for (unsigned i = 0, n = src->getNumResults(); i < n; ++i)
      replacements.push_back(dst->getResult(numDpsBefore + i));
    src->replaceAllUsesWith(replacements);

    dst.setFusionInfoAttr(MOGG::createFusionInfo<MOGG::FusionEpilogueAttr>(
        dst.getContext(), {dst.getOperation(), src.getOperation()},
        {static_cast<uint32_t>(idx)}));
    dst->setLoc(
        mlir::FusedLoc::get(dst.getContext(), {src->getLoc(), dst->getLoc()}));
    src->erase();
    IterOpInterface(dst).dedupeInputs(rewriter);
    return true;
  }
  return false;
}

// The block argument `op`'s body reads its input `in` through. Body args are
// [inputs..., outputs..., index], as MOToMAP builds them.
BlockArgument inputArgFor(IterElementwiseOp op, Value in) {
  return op.getBody().front().getArgument(llvm::find(op.getInputs(), in) -
                                          op.getInputs().begin());
}

// `forwarded`, when set, is one of `a`'s results that `b` reads:
//
//   %x = mo.add(%p, %q)    // a
//   %y = mo.relu(%x)       // b, forwarded = %x
//   mo.output %x, %y       // %x is also read elsewhere
//
// The merged kernel takes no input for `%x`: `b`'s loads of it become the
// value `a` stores to it, and `a`'s store stays for the other readers.
//
// `slice`, when set, is how `b` reads `%x`, `%y = mo.relu(%x[:, 1::2])`: `b`'s
// body then runs in a `map.index.slice.select` at `a`'s index, where the slice
// selects the element, and stores at the slice's index.
//
// Returns the merged kernel, created where `b` was.
IterElementwiseOp fuse(IterElementwiseOp a, IterElementwiseOp b,
                       Value forwarded = {}, SliceIndexOp slice = {}) {
  assert((!slice || forwarded) && "a slice is how `b` reads `forwarded`");
  // Merged inputs: `a`'s, then the ones only `b` carries. A shared operand
  // keeps `a`'s slot, which is what collapses the duplicate load.
  SmallVector<Value> inputs(a.getInputs());
  SmallVector<unsigned> slotForBInput;
  for (auto [i, in] : llvm::enumerate(b.getInputs())) {
    // No slot for the forwarded result, whose loads are replaced below, nor
    // for the slice's bounds, which the select carries statically.
    BlockArgument arg = b.getBody().front().getArgument(i);
    if (in == forwarded || (slice && !arg.use_empty() &&
                            llvm::all_of(arg.getUsers(), [&](Operation *user) {
                              return user == slice.getOperation();
                            }))) {
      slotForBInput.push_back(0);
      continue;
    }
    auto *it = llvm::find(inputs, in);
    slotForBInput.push_back(std::distance(inputs.begin(), it));
    if (it == inputs.end())
      inputs.push_back(in);
  }

  SmallVector<Type> resultTypes(a->getResultTypes());
  llvm::append_range(resultTypes, b->getResultTypes());

  MLIRContext *ctx = a.getContext();
  Location loc = mlir::FusedLoc::get(ctx, {a.getLoc(), b.getLoc()});
  OpBuilder builder(b);
  // Deferred if either member is, as input fusion combines the launch policy.
  auto fused = IterElementwiseOp::create(
      builder, loc, resultTypes, a.getShapeAttr(), inputs,
      /*chain=*/Value(),
      /*fusionInfo=*/
      MOGG::createFusionInfo<MOGG::FusionHorizontalAttr>(
          ctx, {a.getOperation(), b.getOperation()}),
      /*hasReadEffect=*/false, /*hasWriteEffect=*/false,
      /*dispatch=*/
      a.getDispatch() == MOGG::DispatchKind::Deferred ||
              b.getDispatch() == MOGG::DispatchKind::Deferred
          ? MOGG::DispatchKind::Deferred
          : MOGG::DispatchKind::Immediate);

  // `device` and friends are discardable, so `create` does not carry them.
  // The pair shares its device; on any other clash `a`'s attribute wins.
  NamedAttrList attrs(b->getDiscardableAttrDictionary());
  for (NamedAttribute attr : a->getDiscardableAttrs())
    attrs.set(attr.getName(), attr.getValue());
  fused->setDiscardableAttrs(attrs.getDictionary(ctx));

  Block &aBody = a.getBody().front();
  Block *body = &fused.getBody().emplaceBlock();
  for (Value in : inputs)
    body->addArgument(in.getType(), loc);
  for (Type ty : resultTypes)
    body->addArgument(ty, loc);
  body->addArgument(aBody.getArguments().back().getType(), loc);

  OpBuilder bodyBuilder = OpBuilder::atBlockEnd(body);
  BlockArgument index = body->getArguments().back();
  unsigned outputBase = inputs.size();

  IRMapping map;
  BlockArgument forwardedArg = forwarded ? inputArgFor(b, forwarded) : nullptr;
  Value forwardedValue;
  auto cloneBody = [&](IterElementwiseOp src, ArrayRef<unsigned> inputSlots,
                       unsigned firstOutput, OpBuilder &builder,
                       Value srcIndex) {
    // Body args are [inputs..., outputs..., index], as MOToMAP builds them.
    Block &srcBody = src.getBody().front();
    unsigned numInputs = src.getInputs().size();
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < numInputs; ++i)
      map.map(srcBody.getArgument(i), body->getArgument(inputSlots[i]));
    for (unsigned i = 0, e = src->getNumResults(); i < e; ++i)
      map.map(srcBody.getArgument(numInputs + i),
              body->getArgument(outputBase + firstOutput + i));
    map.map(srcBody.getArguments().back(), srcIndex);
    for (Operation &op : srcBody) {
      // A load of the forwarded result is the value `a` just stored.
      auto load = dyn_cast<LoadOp>(op);
      if (load && forwardedArg && load.getTensor() == forwardedArg) {
        map.map(load.getResult(), forwardedValue);
        continue;
      }
      if (slice && &op == slice.getOperation())
        continue;
      builder.clone(op, map);
    }
  };

  SmallVector<unsigned> aSlots(
      llvm::to_vector(llvm::seq<unsigned>(0, a.getInputs().size())));
  cloneBody(a, aSlots, 0, bodyBuilder, index);
  if (forwarded) {
    // `a` stores the result once, at its loop index (see
    // `fuseEscapingConsumer`); `b` loads it only at its own.
    unsigned resultIdx = cast<OpResult>(forwarded).getResultNumber();
    auto store =
        cast<StoreOp>(*aBody.getArgument(a.getInputs().size() + resultIdx)
                           .getUsers()
                           .begin());
    forwardedValue = map.lookup(store.getValue());
  }
  if (slice) {
    auto select =
        SliceSelectOp::create(bodyBuilder, loc, slice.getSpec(), index);
    Block *selectBody = bodyBuilder.createBlock(
        &select.getBody(), select.getBody().end(), {index.getType()}, {loc});
    OpBuilder selectBuilder = OpBuilder::atBlockEnd(selectBody);
    cloneBody(b, slotForBInput, a->getNumResults(), selectBuilder,
              selectBody->getArgument(0));
  } else {
    cloneBody(b, slotForBInput, a->getNumResults(), bodyBuilder, index);
  }

  unsigned split = a->getNumResults();
  a.replaceAllUsesWith(fused.getResults().take_front(split));
  b.replaceAllUsesWith(fused.getResults().drop_front(split));
  b.erase();
  a.erase();
  return fused;
}

// Whether `opaque` reads `value` only through prologues, where prologue
// fusion can recompute its producer instead of loading it.
bool readsOnlyThroughPrologue(IterOpaqueOp opaque, Value value) {
  for (auto [in, arg] :
       llvm::zip(opaque.getInputs(), opaque.getInputBlockArgs()))
    if (in == value &&
        !(arg.hasOneUse() && isa<IterPrologueOp>(*arg.getUsers().begin())))
      return false;
  return true;
}

// The elementwise counterpart of `fuseEscapingReader(IterOpaqueOp &)`:
// `dstKernel`'s result has one foreach consumer, `srcKernel`, and other
// readers too, so input fusion leaves the pair alone. They merge into one
// kernel that stores the result for the other readers and hands `srcKernel`
// the value just computed instead of a reload.
bool fuseEscapingConsumer(IterElementwiseOp dstKernel) {
  if (dstKernel.getChain() || dstKernel.getHasReadEffect() ||
      dstKernel.getHasWriteEffect() || isRaisableViewChain(dstKernel))
    return false;
  Block &dstBody = dstKernel.getBody().front();
  for (auto [k, result] : llvm::enumerate(dstKernel->getResults())) {
    // Returns the one foreach that reads `result`, or null. The merge pays
    // only if `result` stays in memory anyway, because something else reads
    // it:
    //
    //   %x = mo.add(%p, %q)
    //   %y = mo.relu(%x)          // the consumer
    //   mo.output %x, %y          // %x stays stored: merge, relu stops
    //                             // reloading it
    //
    // Not when the other reader is an opaque kernel's prologue:
    //
    //   %b = mo.static.broadcast_to(%p)
    //   %x = mo.add(%b, %q)
    //   %y = mo.relu(%x)
    //   %g = mo.gather(%x, %i)    // later fusion recomputes the add in the
    //                             // relu and in the gather's prologue, so
    //                             // %x is never stored
    //
    // Merging there would store %x where main doesn't, so we skip it, even
    // though for some producers (a plain add) that recompute never happens.
    // Several foreach readers return null too: they merge with each other
    // first.
    // TODO: this guesses whether later fusion would leave `dstKernel`'s
    // result materialized, which is brittle. Fusion should choose between
    // this merge and prologue fusion by comparing what each costs, rather
    // than by predicting what the other pass will do.
    auto getAndCheckConsumerKernel = [&]() -> IterElementwiseOp {
      IterElementwiseOp consumerKernel;
      bool needsStore = false;
      for (OpOperand &use : result.getUses()) {
        Operation *user = use.getOwner();
        bool sameBlock = user->getBlock() == dstKernel->getBlock();
        if (auto consumer = dyn_cast<IterElementwiseOp>(user);
            consumer && sameBlock) {
          if (consumerKernel)
            return nullptr;
          consumerKernel = consumer;
        } else if (auto opaque = dyn_cast<IterOpaqueOp>(user);
                   opaque && sameBlock) {
          needsStore |= !readsOnlyThroughPrologue(opaque, result);
        } else {
          needsStore = true;
        }
      }
      return needsStore ? consumerKernel : nullptr;
    };
    IterElementwiseOp srcKernel = getAndCheckConsumerKernel();
    if (!srcKernel)
      continue;

    // Both kernels run on the same device, and `srcKernel` has no chain or
    // memory effect and isn't a view chain.
    if (MO::getDeviceOrDefault(dstKernel) !=
            MO::getDeviceOrDefault(srcKernel) ||
        srcKernel.getChain() || srcKernel.getHasReadEffect() ||
        srcKernel.getHasWriteEffect() || isRaisableViewChain(srcKernel))
      continue;
    // `srcKernel` takes exactly one input from `dstKernel`, this result, so
    // there is one value to forward.
    if (llvm::count_if(srcKernel.getInputs(), [&](Value in) {
          return in.getDefiningOp() == dstKernel.getOperation();
        }) != 1)
      continue;
    // It reads that input only as `x[i]` at its own loop index, over the same
    // indices: the element iteration i of the merged kernel holds. Or through
    // one strided slice, `x[slice(i)]`, which a select inverts at
    // `dstKernel`'s index.
    Block &srcBody = srcKernel.getBody().front();
    BlockArgument srcIdx = srcBody.getArguments().back();
    BlockArgument fusionArg = inputArgFor(srcKernel, result);
    bool readsAtOwnIndex =
        llvm::all_of(fusionArg.getUsers(), [&](Operation *user) {
          auto load = dyn_cast<LoadOp>(user);
          return load && load->getBlock() == &srcBody &&
                 load.getIndex() == srcIdx;
        });
    SliceIndexOp slice;
    if (!readsAtOwnIndex) {
      slice = matchSelectableSlice(fusionArg, srcIdx, getOutputStores(srcBody),
                                   dstBody.getArguments().back());
      if (!slice)
        continue;
    } else if (dstKernel.getShapeAttr() != srcKernel.getShapeAttr()) {
      continue;
    }
    // `dstKernel` writes the result once, `x[i] = v` at its own loop index;
    // `v` is the value forwarded.
    BlockArgument out = dstBody.getArgument(dstKernel.getInputs().size() + k);
    auto store = out.hasOneUse() ? dyn_cast<StoreOp>(*out.getUsers().begin())
                                 : StoreOp();
    if (!store || store->getBlock() != &dstBody ||
        store.getIndex() != dstBody.getArguments().back())
      continue;

    // The merged kernel takes `srcKernel`'s place, as a sibling merge's does,
    // so nothing in between may read `dstKernel`, and no other operand of
    // `srcKernel` may depend on it.
    if (!resultsUnusedBefore(dstKernel, srcKernel) ||
        llvm::any_of(srcKernel->getOperands(), [&](Value other) {
          return other != result && dataflowGraphDependsOn(other, dstKernel);
        }))
      continue;
    fuse(dstKernel, srcKernel, result, slice);
    return true;
  }
  return false;
}

struct FuseHorizontalPass
    : public MAP::impl::FuseHorizontalBase<FuseHorizontalPass> {
  using Base::Base;
  FuseHorizontalPass(const FuseHorizontalPass &other) : Base(other) {}

  void runOnOperation() override {
    // Fusion stays within a block, so each block runs to its own fixpoint, as
    // in `fuseOutput`. Blocks are not fully independent: a select merge in a
    // branch drops the slice's bounds operands, which can remove the capture
    // an outer pair's cycle check went through, so what fuses can depend on
    // the order blocks are visited in. Every order gives valid IR. Unlike in
    // `fuseOutput`, a block is not sorted first: the greedy choices follow
    // block order.
    getOperation().getBody().walk([&](Block *block) { fuseBlock(*block); });
  }

  void fuseBlock(Block &block) {
    // Pairing can leave a producer one consumer for the merge, and a merge can
    // expose a new pair, so alternate until none of them fuses anything.
    while (true) {
      bool pairedSiblings = fuseSiblings(block);
      bool mergedReaders = fuseEscapingReaders(block);
      bool mergedConsumers = fuseEscapingConsumers(block);
      if (!pairedSiblings && !mergedReaders && !mergedConsumers)
        break;
    }
  }

  // Returns whether any pair was fused.
  bool fuseSiblings(Block &block) {
    // Kernels with the same shape and device that load the same operand form
    // a candidate group, and a kernel joins one group per operand it loads.
    // The groups are built once. One sweep then visits the kernels in block
    // order and fuses each with the first fusible later member of its groups.
    // A fused pair empties `a`'s slot and puts the merged kernel in `b`'s,
    // where `fuse` creates it, so slots stay in block order and the sweep
    // reaches the merged kernel again, to try it against the members after
    // it. Only the pair and the users of its results need new groups;
    // rebuilding every kernel's groups after each pair would rescan the whole
    // block once per fusion.
    //
    // For example, K0..K3 all load %x, so group %x = {K0, K1, K2, K3}, and
    // every pair is fusible:
    //
    //   slot     0     1      2       3
    //   start    K0    K1     K2      K3
    //   i = 0    -     K01    K2      K3       fuse(K0, K1) into slot 1
    //   i = 1    -     -      K012    K3       fuse(K01, K2) into slot 2
    //   i = 2    -     -      -       K0123    fuse(K012, K3) into slot 3
    //
    // The sweep goes kernel by kernel, not group by group: kernels of other
    // groups between these slots are visited as the sweep reaches them, and
    // groups are patched after every fusion, not rebuilt once a group is
    // done. The sweep never revisits earlier kernels: a merged kernel reads
    // everything both members read, so every pair rejected before it is still
    // rejected.
    SmallVector<IterElementwiseOp> kernels =
        llvm::to_vector(block.getOps<IterElementwiseOp>());
    DenseMap<Operation *, unsigned> slotOf;

    // A pair that shares no group fails `fusible`, so a kernel is tried only
    // against the later kernels of its own groups. They are still visited in
    // block order, which the greedy choice depends on.
    SmallVector<SmallVector<FusionCandidateGroup>> groupsOf(kernels.size());
    DenseMap<std::tuple<Attribute, Attribute, Value>, SmallVector<unsigned>>
        members;
    auto addGroups = [&](unsigned slot) {
      groupsOf[slot] = fusionCandidateGroupsOf(kernels[slot]);
      for (const FusionCandidateGroup &group : groupsOf[slot])
        members[group.key()].push_back(slot);
    };
    auto dropGroups = [&](unsigned slot) {
      for (const FusionCandidateGroup &group : groupsOf[slot])
        llvm::erase(members[group.key()], slot);
      groupsOf[slot].clear();
    };
    for (auto [slot, kernel] : llvm::enumerate(kernels)) {
      slotOf[kernel] = slot;
      addGroups(slot);
    }

    bool fusedAny = false;
    for (unsigned i = 0, e = kernels.size(); i < e; ++i) {
      if (!kernels[i])
        continue;
      SmallVector<unsigned> candidates;
      for (const FusionCandidateGroup &group : groupsOf[i])
        for (unsigned j : members.at(group.key()))
          if (j > i)
            candidates.push_back(j);
      llvm::sort(candidates);
      candidates.erase(llvm::unique(candidates), candidates.end());
      for (unsigned j : candidates) {
        IterElementwiseOp a = kernels[i];
        IterElementwiseOp b = kernels[j];
        if (!fusible(a, b))
          continue;
        // Users of the pair's results load the merged kernel's results after
        // the fusion, which changes their groups.
        llvm::SetVector<unsigned> users;
        for (IterElementwiseOp member : {a, b})
          for (Operation *user : member->getUsers())
            if (auto it = slotOf.find(user); it != slotOf.end())
              users.insert(it->second);
        users.remove(i);
        users.remove(j);
        for (unsigned slot : users)
          dropGroups(slot);
        dropGroups(i);
        dropGroups(j);
        slotOf.erase(a);
        slotOf.erase(b);

        IterElementwiseOp merged = fuse(a, b);
        kernels[i] = nullptr;
        kernels[j] = merged;
        slotOf[merged] = j;
        addGroups(j);
        for (unsigned slot : users)
          addGroups(slot);
        ++numKernelsFused;
        fusedAny = true;
        break;
      }
    }
    return fusedAny;
  }

  // Returns whether any consumer was merged.
  bool fuseEscapingReaders(Block &block) {
    bool mergedAny = false;
    // Merging a consumer into a producer's epilogue rebuilds the producer, so
    // the scan restarts after each one.
    bool merged = true;
    while (merged) {
      merged = false;
      auto opaques = llvm::to_vector(block.getOps<IterOpaqueOp>());
      for (IterOpaqueOp dst : opaques) {
        if (fuseEscapingReader(dst)) {
          ++numKernelsFused;
          merged = true;
          mergedAny = true;
          break;
        }
      }
    }
    return mergedAny;
  }

  // Returns whether any consumer was merged.
  bool fuseEscapingConsumers(Block &block) {
    bool mergedAny = false;
    // A merge replaces both kernels, so the scan restarts after each one.
    bool merged = true;
    while (merged) {
      merged = false;
      for (IterElementwiseOp dst :
           llvm::to_vector(block.getOps<IterElementwiseOp>())) {
        if (fuseEscapingConsumer(dst)) {
          ++numKernelsFused;
          merged = true;
          mergedAny = true;
          break;
        }
      }
    }
    return mergedAny;
  }

  Statistic numKernelsFused{this, "num-kernels-fused",
                            "Number of kernels fused"};
};

using namespace M;

namespace M::MAP {

#define GEN_PASS_DEF_FUSEINPUT
#include "GraphCompiler/MAPDialect/Transforms/MAPTransforms.h.inc"

bool isViewForeach(IterElementwiseOp op) {
  return op.getBody()
      .walk([&](IndexTransformOpInterface) { return WalkResult::interrupt(); })
      .wasInterrupted();
}

bool producesThroughView(StoreOp store) {
  return dataflowGraphContains<WalkDirection::Producers>(
      store.getValue().getDefiningOp(),
      [](Operation *o) { return isa<IndexTransformOpInterface>(o); });
}

bool isPureViewForeach(IterElementwiseOp op) {
  return isViewForeach(op) &&
         !op.getBody()
              .walk([&](CallElementwiseOp) { return WalkResult::interrupt(); })
              .wasInterrupted();
}

// Above this many elements, re-reading a tensor operand is expensive.
constexpr int64_t kLargeTensorElementThreshold = 4096;

static bool isLargeTensorOperand(Type type) {
  auto tensorType = dyn_cast<MO::TensorType>(type);
  if (!tensorType)
    return false;
  std::optional<int64_t> numElements = tensorType.getNumElements();
  return !numElements.has_value() ||
         *numElements > kLargeTensorElementThreshold;
}

bool isCheapToDuplicate(IterElementwiseOp op) {
  int numLargeOperands = 0;
  for (Value input : op.getInputs())
    if (isLargeTensorOperand(input.getType()))
      if (++numLargeOperands > 1)
        return false;
  return true;
}

bool loadIndexCrossesReshape(LoadOp load) {
  return dataflowGraphContains<WalkDirection::Producers>(
      load.getIndex().getDefiningOp(),
      [](Operation *o) { return isa<ReshapeIndexOp>(o); });
}

bool anyLoadCrossesReshape(Value tensor) {
  return llvm::any_of(tensor.getUsers(), [](Operation *user) {
    auto load = dyn_cast<LoadOp>(user);
    return load && loadIndexCrossesReshape(load);
  });
}

namespace {

// TODO(GEX-4184): support multiple stores/outputs, which only arise via
// sibling fusion.
StoreOp producerStoreOf(IterElementwiseOp src) {
  return getUniqueStore(src.getBody().front());
}

// Guards against fusing across a chain-carrying kernel (e.g. mo.mutable.store)
// when doing so could change effective ordering relative to another consumer of
// the same chain.
bool checkMutableKernelFusible(Value srcInChain, Value srcOutChain,
                               Value dstInChain, Value dstOutChain) {
  if (srcInChain && srcOutChain && dstInChain && dstOutChain) {
    if (dstInChain != srcOutChain)
      return false;
    if (!srcOutChain.hasOneUse())
      return false;
  }
  if (dstInChain && !dstInChain.hasOneUse())
    return false;
  return true;
}

// The prologue capturing `dst`'s `argIdx`'th input and the capture's index, or
// null unless the input's only user is a prologue whose capture's only use is
// a load. Epilogue captures are reached through output fusion instead.
struct ClosureCapture {
  CapturingFusionClosure closure = nullptr;
  unsigned captureIdx = 0;
};

ClosureCapture findExistingPrologueCapture(IterOpaqueOp dst, unsigned argIdx) {
  BlockArgument dstArg = dst.getInputBlockArgs()[argIdx];
  if (!dstArg.hasOneUse())
    return {};
  auto closure = dyn_cast<CapturingFusionClosure>(*dstArg.getUsers().begin());
  if (!closure || !isa<IterPrologueOp>(closure.getOperation()))
    return {};
  auto captureIt = llvm::find(closure.getCaptures(), dstArg);
  if (captureIt == closure.getCaptures().end())
    return {};
  unsigned captureIdx =
      static_cast<unsigned>(captureIt - closure.getCaptures().begin());
  BlockArgument capArg = closure.getCaptureBlockArgs()[captureIdx];
  if (!capArg.hasOneUse())
    return {};
  // E.g. dynamic `map.index.slice` bounds have no load site.
  if (!isa<LoadOp>(*capArg.getUsers().begin()))
    return {};
  return {closure, captureIdx};
}

// An opaque consumer carries no device, so the result's tensor type stands in.
bool sameDevice(IterElementwiseOp src, Operation *dst) {
  auto srcDev = MO::getDeviceOrDefault(src);
  if (auto dstForeach = dyn_cast<IterElementwiseOp>(dst))
    return MO::getDeviceOrDefault(dstForeach) == srcDev;
  auto tensorTy = dyn_cast<MO::TensorType>(src.getResult(0).getType());
  return tensorTy && MO::getDeviceOrDefault(tensorTy) == srcDev;
}

// The first load of `src`'s result in `dst`, the site `shouldFuse` inspects.
LoadOp firstConsumerLoad(IterElementwiseOp dst, IterElementwiseOp src) {
  Block &body = dst.getBody().front();
  for (auto [i, input] : llvm::enumerate(dst.getInputs())) {
    if (input != src.getResult(0))
      continue;
    for (Operation *user : body.getArgument(i).getUsers())
      if (auto load = dyn_cast<LoadOp>(user))
        return load;
  }
  return nullptr;
}

// Folds the loads of `tensor` that read the same index in the same block into
// the first of them, as CSE would.
void mergeRedundantLoads(BlockArgument tensor, mlir::RewriterBase &rewriter) {
  DenseMap<std::pair<Block *, Value>, LoadOp> first;
  for (Operation *user : llvm::to_vector(tensor.getUsers())) {
    auto load = cast<LoadOp>(user);
    auto [it, inserted] =
        first.try_emplace({load->getBlock(), load.getIndex()}, load);
    if (inserted)
      continue;
    LoadOp kept = it->second;
    if (load->isBeforeInBlock(kept))
      std::swap(load, kept);
    rewriter.replaceAllUsesWith(load.getResult(), kept.getResult());
    rewriter.eraseOp(load);
    it->second = kept;
  }
}

// Splices `src` into `dst` and records it as a view or elementwise fusion.
void spliceIntoForeach(IterElementwiseOp dst, IterElementwiseOp src,
                       PatternRewriter &rewriter) {
  bool isView = producesThroughView(producerStoreOf(src));
  spliceProducer(dst, src, rewriter);

  if (isView)
    dst.setFusionInfoAttr(MOGG::createFusionInfo<MOGG::FusionViewAttr>(
        src->getContext(), {src, dst}));
  else
    dst.setFusionInfoAttr(MOGG::createFusionInfo<MOGG::FusionElementwiseAttr>(
        src->getContext(), {src, dst}));
  dst->setLoc(
      mlir::FusedLoc::get(src->getContext(), {src->getLoc(), dst->getLoc()}));
  dst.setHasReadEffect(src.getHasReadEffect() || dst.getHasReadEffect());
  dst.setHasWriteEffect(src.getHasWriteEffect() || dst.getHasWriteEffect());
  // `dst` keeps its own launch policy, as on the old path: a sync-launch
  // consumer such as a transpose (GEX-2569) must not turn async.
}

// Splices `src`'s body into `dst`'s existing prologue behind the captures
// `src` feeds.
void spliceIntoClosure(IterOpaqueOp dst, IterElementwiseOp src,
                       PatternRewriter &rewriter) {
  SmallVector<unsigned> fusionIndices;
  for (auto [i, input] : llvm::enumerate(dst.getInputs()))
    if (input == src.getResult(0))
      fusionIndices.push_back(i);
  assert(!fusionIndices.empty() && "src must be a current input of dst");

  unsigned numSrcInputs = src.getInputs().size();

  for (unsigned argIdx : llvm::reverse(fusionIndices)) {
    ClosureCapture capture = findExistingPrologueCapture(dst, argIdx);
    assert(capture.closure && "findEligibleProducer should have verified this");
    CapturingFusionClosure closure = capture.closure;
    // Captured before cloning inserts a second block ahead of it.
    Block &closureBody = closure.getBody().front();

    BlockArgument oldCap = closure.getCaptureBlockArgs()[capture.captureIdx];
    auto oldLoad = cast<LoadOp>(*oldCap.getUsers().begin());
    Value loadIndex = oldLoad.getIndex();

    rewriter.cloneRegionBefore(src.getBody(), closure.getBody(),
                               closure.getBody().begin());
    Block &srcClone = closure.getBody().front();

    auto storeOp = getUniqueStore(srcClone);
    Value fusedVal = storeOp.getValue();
    storeOp.erase();
    srcClone.eraseArgument(numSrcInputs);

    SmallVector<Value> fusedArgs;
    for (Value input : src.getInputs()) {
      unsigned dstInputIdx = dst.getInputs().size();
      dst.insertInputsAt(dstInputIdx, input);
      Value dstInputArg = dst.getInputBlockArgs()[dstInputIdx];
      closure.appendCaptureOperand(dstInputArg);
      fusedArgs.push_back(
          closureBody.addArgument(input.getType(), input.getLoc()));
    }
    fusedArgs.push_back(loadIndex);

    rewriter.inlineBlockBefore(&srcClone, oldLoad, fusedArgs);

    oldLoad.getResult().replaceAllUsesWith(fusedVal);
    oldLoad.erase();
    closure.eraseCaptureAt(capture.captureIdx);
    dst.eraseInputsAt(argIdx);

    dst.setFusionInfoAttr(MOGG::createFusionInfo<MOGG::FusionPrologueAttr>(
        src->getContext(), {src, dst}, {argIdx}));
    dst->setLoc(
        mlir::FusedLoc::get(src->getContext(), {src->getLoc(), dst->getLoc()}));
  }

  // `dst` keeps its own launch policy, as on the old path: a sync-launch
  // consumer such as a transpose (GEX-2569) must not turn async.
}

// Whether `dstOp` has a site to read `src`'s result through AND `shouldFuse`
// accepts it. Without the latter, duplication would clone `src` into some users
// while another (e.g. an opaque, for the elementwise fuser) keeps it
// materialized -- pure recomputation.
bool hasFusionSite(IterElementwiseOp src, Operation *dstOp,
                   const InputFusionConfig &config) {
  if (src->getBlock() != dstOp->getBlock())
    return false;

  if (auto dst = dyn_cast<IterElementwiseOp>(dstOp)) {
    LoadOp load = firstConsumerLoad(dst, src);
    return load && config.shouldFuse(producerStoreOf(src), load);
  }

  auto dst = dyn_cast<IterOpaqueOp>(dstOp);
  if (!dst)
    return false;
  bool feedsInput = false;
  for (auto [i, in] : llvm::enumerate(dst.getInputs())) {
    if (in != src.getResult(0))
      continue;
    ClosureCapture capture = findExistingPrologueCapture(dst, i);
    if (!capture.closure)
      return false;
    BlockArgument capArg =
        capture.closure.getCaptureBlockArgs()[capture.captureIdx];
    if (capArg.use_empty())
      return false;
    auto load = dyn_cast<LoadOp>(*capArg.getUsers().begin());
    if (!load || !config.shouldFuse(producerStoreOf(src), load))
      return false;
    feedsInput = true;
  }
  return feedsInput;
}

// Duplication pays only by removing the materialization, so every user must
// absorb the clone; `mo.output`, or an opaque with no prologue on that input,
// keeps it in memory anyway.
bool duplicationAllowed(IterElementwiseOp src,
                        const InputFusionConfig &config) {
  if (src.getResult(0).hasOneUse())
    return true;
  for (Operation *user : src.getResult(0).getUsers())
    if (!hasFusionSite(src, user, config))
      return false;
  return config.canDuplicate(src);
}

// An eligible producer feeding `dstOp`, or null. A producer feeding several
// inputs must clear all of them, since the splice fuses them all.
IterElementwiseOp findEligibleProducer(Operation *dstOp,
                                       const InputFusionConfig &config) {
  if (auto dst = dyn_cast<IterElementwiseOp>(dstOp)) {
    Block &body = dst.getBody().front();
    DenseSet<Operation *> tried;
    // Fusing a producer moves it when `dst` is its only reader and copies it
    // otherwise. Take the single-use ones first: once `d = tanh(r)` is in,
    // `dst` is `r`'s only reader and `r` moves too. Taking `r` first copies it,
    // then copies it again inside `d`, doubling per level of such a chain.
    IterElementwiseOp duplicable;
    for (Value input : dst.getInputs()) {
      auto src = input.getDefiningOp<IterElementwiseOp>();
      if (!src || src.getNumResults() != 1 || !tried.insert(src).second)
        continue;
      // Fusion stays within a block: never across a control-flow boundary.
      if (src->getBlock() != dstOp->getBlock())
        continue;
      if (!sameDevice(src, dst) || !duplicationAllowed(src, config))
        continue;
      if (!checkMutableKernelFusible(src.getInputChain(), src.getOutputChain(),
                                     dst.getInputChain(), dst.getOutputChain()))
        continue;
      // Reshape barrier: a view cannot fuse into a load already past a reshape.
      if (llvm::any_of(llvm::enumerate(dst.getInputs()), [&](auto input) {
            return input.value() == src.getResult(0) &&
                   anyLoadCrossesReshape(body.getArgument(input.index()));
          }))
        continue;
      LoadOp load = firstConsumerLoad(dst, src);
      if (!load || !config.shouldFuse(producerStoreOf(src), load))
        continue;
      if (src.getResult(0).hasOneUse())
        return src;
      if (!duplicable)
        duplicable = src;
    }
    return duplicable;
  }

  auto dst = cast<IterOpaqueOp>(dstOp);
  DenseSet<Operation *> tried;
  // Highest operand index first, so erasing a fused input never shifts an
  // index still to be stamped into `operandIndices`.
  for (Value input : llvm::reverse(dst.getInputs())) {
    auto src = input.getDefiningOp<IterElementwiseOp>();
    if (!src || src.getNumResults() != 1 || !tried.insert(src).second)
      continue;
    if (src->getBlock() != dstOp->getBlock())
      continue;
    if (!sameDevice(src, dst) || !duplicationAllowed(src, config))
      continue;
    bool ok = true;
    LoadOp firstLoad = nullptr;
    for (auto [i, in] : llvm::enumerate(dst.getInputs())) {
      if (in != src.getResult(0))
        continue;
      ClosureCapture capture = findExistingPrologueCapture(dst, i);
      if (!capture.closure) {
        ok = false;
        break;
      }
      BlockArgument capArg =
          capture.closure.getCaptureBlockArgs()[capture.captureIdx];
      auto load = cast<LoadOp>(*capArg.getUsers().begin());
      if (loadIndexCrossesReshape(load)) {
        ok = false;
        break;
      }
      if (!firstLoad)
        firstLoad = load;
    }
    if (ok && firstLoad && config.shouldFuse(producerStoreOf(src), firstLoad))
      return src;
  }
  return nullptr;
}

} // namespace

void spliceProducer(IterOpInterface dst, IterElementwiseOp src,
                    mlir::RewriterBase &rewriter) {
  assert(isa<StructuredIterOpInterface>(dst.getOperation()) &&
         "an opaque kernel reads its inputs through closures, not loads");
  Region &dstRegion = dst->getRegion(0);
  Block &dstBody = dstRegion.front();
  unsigned numSrcInputs = src.getInputs().size();

  SmallVector<unsigned> fusionIndices;
  for (auto [i, input] : llvm::enumerate(dst.getInputs()))
    if (input == src.getResult(0))
      fusionIndices.push_back(i);
  assert(!fusionIndices.empty() && "src must be a current input of dst");

  for (unsigned argIdx : llvm::reverse(fusionIndices)) {
    dst.insertInputsAt(argIdx, src.getInputs());
    ValueRange newDstArgs = dstBody.getArguments().slice(argIdx, numSrcInputs);
    BlockArgument oldTensorArg = dstBody.getArgument(argIdx + numSrcInputs);

    // One load per index, so `src` is cloned once per value it computes; a
    // clone per load doubles the body at every fan-out level.
    mergeRedundantLoads(oldTensorArg, rewriter);
    for (Operation *user : llvm::to_vector(oldTensorArg.getUsers())) {
      auto load = cast<LoadOp>(user);
      rewriter.cloneRegionBefore(src.getBody(), dstRegion, dstRegion.begin());
      Block &srcClone = dstRegion.front();

      StoreOp storeOp = getUniqueStore(srcClone);
      Value fusedVal = storeOp.getValue();
      rewriter.eraseOp(storeOp);
      srcClone.eraseArgument(numSrcInputs);

      // Before `load`, so dst's own transform chain dominates.
      SmallVector<Value> fusedArgs(newDstArgs.begin(), newDstArgs.end());
      fusedArgs.push_back(load.getIndex());
      rewriter.inlineBlockBefore(&srcClone, load, fusedArgs);
      rewriter.replaceOp(load, fusedVal);
    }

    dst.eraseInputsAt(argIdx + numSrcInputs, 1);
  }
}

unsigned fuseInput(MO::GraphOp graphOp, const InputFusionConfig &config) {
  PatternRewriter rewriter(graphOp.getContext());

  // Kernels live in the graph body and in any nested control-flow regions (an
  // `mo.if`'s branches); a producer/consumer edge is always within one block.
  llvm::SmallSetVector<Block *, 8> blocks;
  graphOp.getBody().walk([&](Operation *op) {
    if (isa<IterElementwiseOp, IterOpaqueOp>(op))
      blocks.insert(op->getBlock());
  });

  // Consumers bottom-up, so each consumer's producer chain drains in one visit.
  MO::ParametricTopologyAnalysis topo(graphOp);
  DenseSet<Operation *> erased;
  unsigned numFused = 0;
  for (Block *block : blocks) {
    SmallVector<Operation *> ops;
    for (Operation &op : *block)
      ops.push_back(&op);
    topo.computeTopologicalSorting(ops);

    for (Operation *op : llvm::reverse(ops)) {
      if (erased.contains(op) || !isa<IterElementwiseOp, IterOpaqueOp>(op))
        continue;
      uint64_t fusedIntoConsumer = 0;
      while (IterElementwiseOp src = findEligibleProducer(op, config)) {
        // The cap bounds duplication; moving a sole-use producer adds no work.
        bool duplicates = !src.getResult(0).hasOneUse();
        if (duplicates && fusedIntoConsumer >= config.maxFusionSetSize)
          break;
        if (isa<IterElementwiseOp>(op))
          spliceIntoForeach(cast<IterElementwiseOp>(op), src, rewriter);
        else
          spliceIntoClosure(cast<IterOpaqueOp>(op), src, rewriter);
        if (src.getResult(0).use_empty()) {
          erased.insert(src);
          src->erase();
        }
        // Uniquing inputs re-exposes a shared producer as single-use, so this
        // drain fuses it once instead of duplicating or dropping it.
        cast<IterOpInterface>(op).dedupeInputs(rewriter);
        fusedIntoConsumer += duplicates;
        ++numFused;
      }
    }
  }
  return numFused;
}

namespace {

// Unconstrained input fusion (fuse every eligible edge). For testing.
struct FuseInputPass : public MAP::impl::FuseInputBase<FuseInputPass> {
  using Base::Base;

  void runOnOperation() override {
    InputFusionConfig config;
    config.shouldFuse = [](StoreOp, LoadOp) { return true; };
    config.canDuplicate = [](IterElementwiseOp) { return true; };
    fuseInput(getOperation(), config);
  }
};

} // namespace

} // namespace M::MAP
